clue.text: Are Wolves retaining European champion footballer?

indicators.note: retaining means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: to be wolves, i.e. to wolf food down, is to gorge
champion as an adjective means best, top of the field

explanation.surface: A football fan asks whether Wolverhampton Wanderers are keeping hold of a European title-winning player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wolves' looks like the football club but is the verb: to wolf is to gorge. 'retaining' puts E inside GORGE to give GEORGE.
explanation.definitionFit: George Best was the celebrated Manchester United and Northern Ireland winger, a European Cup winner in 1968.

clue.text: Objects to mail being held in the sticks

indicators.note: being held in means the mail sits inside the objects

parts.note: objects means aims, goals
post is mail

explanation.surface: Letters are kept out in the remote countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the sticks' looks like rural backwoods but is football slang for the goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticks is sports slang for the posts of a goal, between which the goalkeeper stands.

clue.text: This is sweet nothings interspersed with flirts regularly

indicators.note: interspersed with means the two sets of letters are mixed in among each other

parts.note: each nothing is a zero, the letter O, and there are four of them

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of flirts

explanation.surface: A dessert is described as sweet nothings scattered among flirtations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks LRS from flirts; 'interspersed with' sets them between the four Os.
explanation.definitionFit: Oloroso is a dark sherry often sweetened, served as a sweet wine.

clue.text: Quartet addressed, before audience, elevated road transport

indicators.note: before an audience means said aloud, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: speaking to a group of four, one calls them you four

indicators.note: elevated means lifted up, read upwards in a down clue

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, written AI

explanation.surface: A quartet is spoken to before an audience about a raised road or rail line.
explanation.walkthrough: Addressing a quartet you might say 'you four'. The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; 'elevated' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Transport in the sense of rapture or overwhelming joy is a synonym for intense elation.

clue.text: The RA following this major?

parts.note: the words The RA are the letters of earth shattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark about the Royal Academy following an important event.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: break up EARTH and THE RA follows. RA stands for the Royal Academy, which surface readers may take it for.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth-shattering means of huge importance, so it fits major in the sense of momentous.

clue.text: Well-equipped to take on champ and upset also, in your case

parts.note: too means also
thy is the old possessive form for your, used in the familiar thou case

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to face the champion and upset them too, in your view.
explanation.walkthrough: To champ is to chew noisily, which takes plenty of teeth. 'and upset' seems to serve the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Having plenty of large teeth leaves a creature well equipped to chew or chomp.

clue.text: Platform where solution is read out

indicators.note: read out signals that the word is spoken, so we want something sounding like it

parts.note: the key to a puzzle is its solution

explanation.surface: Someone asks at which platform the answer will be announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read out' turns KEY, a synonym of 'solution', into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A quay is a landing platform alongside water where boats load and unload.

clue.text: Roman who supports holding arms for collaborators

parts.note: qui is Latin for who
slings are supports that hold injured arms

explanation.surface: A Roman who props up the military wins over traitors.
explanation.walkthrough: Vidkun Quisling led Norway's Nazi puppet government, and his name came to mean any traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Quislings are traitors who collaborate with an occupying enemy.

clue.text: One pulled at bar, woman's a catch

parts.note: a pint of ale is pulled by the bartender from a hand pump
a wife is a woman, especially a married one

explanation.surface: A woman is a good catch at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch' suggests a desirable partner, but it is a fish a fisherman lands.
explanation.definitionFit: The alewife is a North American fish of the herring family, something an angler might land.

clue.text: Vets initially record that a pig's eating more than expected

indicators.note: eating means the pig takes the following letters inside it

parts.note: a boar is a male pig

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of the following word

parts.note: an EP (extended play) is a type of record

explanation.surface: Vets note that a pig is eating more than they predicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives V from Vets; 'eating' puts the V and the record inside the pig, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Above par is an idiom for better than the normal or expected level, from the golf and stock-market sense of par.

clue.text: Hardy hero's last survivor

indicators.note: last means take only the final letter of the word hero

parts.note: a liver is one who lives, so in a whimsical sense a survivor

explanation.surface: The hero of a Thomas Hardy novel is the last one left alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' suggests Thomas Hardy, but it is Oliver Hardy of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver was the first name of Hardy, the larger half of the film comedy double act Laurel and Hardy.

clue.text: One holding chair against piano?

parts.note: one holding a university chair is a senior academic; read 'against piano' through opposites, each word swapped for its musical or debating contrary, to get the short title

explanation.surface: A pianist's stool is held up against the instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The opposite of 'against' is 'for' (PRO), and the opposite of piano (soft) is forte, F in music: together the short name for a professor.
explanation.definitionFit: A professor holds a chair, the formal title of a senior university post, and prof is the colloquial short form.

clue.text: Viewer's tossing him a cloth containing coin

indicators.note: containing means the rearranged letters hold the coin inside them
tossing throws the letters of these words into a new order

parts.note: p, a penny, is a small British coin

explanation.surface: Someone throws a man a cloth with a coin wrapped in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossing' rearranges the letters into OHTHALMIC; 'containing' then slips the penny in as the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophthalmic means relating to the eye, and the eye is the organ a viewer sees with.

clue.text: Modest when accepting trophy and fame

indicators.note: accepting means the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: slight means small or modest in size
a pot is slang for a sports trophy or cup

explanation.surface: A modest person accepts an award and the fame that comes with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is only a link; the trophy is a pot, as in a cup won at sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the spotlight means being the centre of public attention, so the word stands for fame.

clue.text: Raft trips with rum to river factory

indicators.note: trips means stumbles, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Rafting holidays with plenty of rum heading off to a riverside plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trips' rearranges RAFT, RUM and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish farm produces fish for market, here a river fish raised in tanks as in a factory.

clue.text: Go down with unspecified number in boat

indicators.note: in means the number is placed inside the boat

parts.note: keel is used for the bottom of a boat, and a keel is also a flat-bottomed barge
n stands for an unspecified number in mathematics

explanation.surface: Instructions for a group getting down low in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts N inside KEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To kneel is to go down onto one's knees, a lowering of the body.

clue.text: Mark, doing half of what he's asked?

definitions.text: Mark, doing half of what he's asked?

parts.words: Mark, doing half of what he's asked?
parts.note: Mark Antony asks Friends, Romans, countrymen to give him their ears; doing half means offering just one

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark only does half of what he is told.
explanation.walkthrough: From Shakespeare's Julius Caesar: Mark Antony asks the crowd to lend me your ears; one of the pair is half the request.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend an ear is an idiom meaning to listen sympathetically, here half of a request for both ears.

clue.text: First sight of spring brings future leaders' pledge

definitions.meaning: the source of a spring, where water first appears from the ground
people who will lead promise we will be in charge, written with an apostrophe

explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season, but it is a spring of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellhead is the source of a spring or stream, and the contraction we'll head is a pledge to lead in future.

clue.text: Dismiss boy speaking German

indicators.note: speaking signals that the words are said aloud to give a sound-alike

parts.note: dismiss is sack and boy is son, run together as one spoken phrase

explanation.surface: An instruction to fire a lad who talks in German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaking' turns SACK SON into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A Saxon is a native of Saxony, a German state, or of the Germanic people who settled England.

clue.text: Rave over, grown-up confiscates a tablet

indicators.note: confiscates means the grown-up takes the a and holds it inside

parts.note: an adult is a grown-up
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: At a rave, an adult takes away a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rave' suggests a dance party with pills, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulate is to praise excessively, which is what to rave over something means.

clue.text: Stealth not normally found in an ancient king

indicators.note: found in means the rearranged letters sit inside the short word
not normally means the letters of stealth appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A remark that stealth is not a trait usually seen in an old monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not normally' rearranges the letters of the first word into THELSTA, which 'found in' places inside the final two words' letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Athelstan was the tenth-century Anglo-Saxon king often called the first king of England.

clue.text: Country school getting royal visit

indicators.note: visit means the royal goes inside the school

parts.note: to school someone is to train them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A country school is honoured by a royal visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is a verb here, and 'visit' tells us the Queen goes into it; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Country can mean a stretch of land of some character, which is what terrain means.

clue.text: Too many tablets containing commandments upset a chap

indicators.note: containing means the overdose holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: OD is an overdose, taking too many pills

indicators.note: upset means turned over, read upwards in a down clue

parts.note: laws are commandments

explanation.surface: Moses, with too many tablets of commandments, drops them on a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the commandments upward, giving SWAL; 'containing' places that inside the overdose.
explanation.definitionFit: Oswald is a man's name, so it stands for a chap in crossword style.

clue.text: Simply too desirable!

parts.note: simply and just both mean merely
as well means too, also

explanation.surface: An exclamation that something is just too lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'too desirable' is one phrase; it splits so that 'too' gives AS WELL and 'desirable' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying it is just as well means it is fortunate or desirable that something happened.

clue.text: Killer in deep yellow approaching

parts.note: or is gold, the deep yellow tincture in heraldry
ca (circa) means about, approximately, so approaching a figure

explanation.surface: A murderer is spotted in a dark yellow coat, coming closer.
explanation.walkthrough: Heraldry calls gold 'or'; circa, used before approximate dates, means about, close to.
explanation.definitionFit: The orca is known as the killer whale, a top predator of the oceans.

clue.text: Last letter a postman's given a revolutionary

parts.note: z is the last letter of the alphabet
Postman Pat is a British children's TV postman

explanation.surface: A postman delivers a final letter to a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: Postman Pat is the hero of a long-running British children's TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Emiliano Zapata was a leader of the Mexican Revolution, so a classic example of a revolutionary.

clue.text: Use blade to go and remove head from tasty fish

indicators.note: remove head from means the first letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: nice means tasty and a skate is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Cooking instructions: take a knife, cut the head off a delicious fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remove head from' drops N from NICE SKATE. 'blade' suggests a kitchen knife, but it is the blade of a skate.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice-skate is to move over ice on a skate, which runs on a narrow metal blade.

clue.text: Possibility in pool to make waves

definitions.meaning: in the football pools a permutation is one of the combinations of results chosen
to give hair a long-lasting wave by chemical treatment

explanation.walkthrough: The football pools are a British weekly betting game on match results.
explanation.definitionFit: Perm is short for permutation, a set of selections in the pools, and for permanent wave, a curled hairstyle.

clue.text: Mess setter has to put away?

definitions.meaning: a muddle or shambles, in British slang
a setter is a breed of dog, so its meal is what it must eat up

explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword setter, but it is the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog's dinner is British slang for a shambles, and literally the meal a setter, a gun dog, eats up.
